trust_decision.summary: In add-on mode the settings/policy handlers must be invoked only when the transport peer is the Supervisor ingress address (172.30.32.2); every other caller must present the MCP secret path. The decision belongs at mount time in register_settings_routes, not inside the handlers, because the identical handler objects are also mounted under secret_prefix for legitimate direct/remote access.

landing_point.why: The only place where add-on mode mounts the settings/policy routes at the bare root; the report's "bare root path" leads here, and the 24-row table right above it is the natural second thing to edit.

fix_sites.entry_point: GET / (add-on root settings page served by the HA ingress "Open Web UI" button)
fix_sites.module_kind: http_route_registration (FastMCP custom route, registered outside the route table)

fix_sites.entry_point: bare-root mount of the 24 settings/policy routes: /settings, /api/settings/{tools,restart,info,features,advanced,backups,backup-config}, /api/policy/{config,pending,approve,deny,tool-schema,value-source}

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site and no O8 route exist; the only reason-to-dismiss lever sits on the root mount itself: the pinned comment at src/ha_mcp/settings_ui.py:3038-3042 says direct port-9583 LAN access to these routes is part of the existing add-on networking model where the secret path is the auth for direct access, and asks only that it be documented in DOCS.md (homeassistant-addon/DOCS.md:372-376 likewise treats LAN access as normal and only forbids internet exposure).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Direct/remote clients (Docker/standalone, tunnels) authenticate with the MCP secret path, so the secret-prefix mount of the same handler objects must keep answering 200; and the stdio sidecar's standalone Starlette app serves the same handlers on 127.0.0.1 with its own random secret path, Host and Origin checks. A guard placed inside the shared handlers themselves (rather than at the add-on root mount) 403s both of these legitimate callers, and a guard that also rejects the Supervisor peer breaks the "Open Web UI" button.

O6_input_shapes: all 24 table entries mounted at the bare root (per path+method: settings page, tools GET/POST, restart POST, info GET, features GET/POST, advanced GET/POST, backups GET/DELETE and per-name GET/diff GET/restore POST/delete DELETE, backup-config GET/POST, policy config GET/PUT, pending GET, approve POST, deny POST, tool-schema GET, value-source GET)
the separately registered bare-root "/" page that is not in the route table
a request with no client info (request.client is None) rather than an address
a forged X-Forwarded-For header claiming 172.30.32.2 from a non-Supervisor peer
requests arriving under the secret prefix, which must stay unguarded

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A bare-root (no secret prefix) mount of the sidecar's hand-maintained settings/policy Route list.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The sidecar duplicates the settings route table by hand and predates the one-table consolidation in register_settings_routes (commit b39b5adf); a maintainer adding a short "open the UI at 127.0.0.1:PORT/" convenience would add exactly this route set with no secret prefix.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: register_browser_landing mounted at "/" as well as at the MCP secret path.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is already a GET-only custom route registered outside the settings table and outside RequireAuthMiddleware; a maintainer wanting a friendly front door for browsers on the published port would pass "/" instead of the secret path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A proxy mode that forwards the request sub-path to the target root instead of only to the secret target_url.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The webhook proxy already registers an unauthenticated GET/POST webhook whose id is the only credential; forwarding sub-paths is the obvious next feature request for proxying the settings UI, and the forwarding code at __init__.py:311 uses target_url verbatim so a root-forwarding variant would reach the bare root as a non-Supervisor peer.

O9_family: Missing authentication / authorization on administrative HTTP routes (CWE-306), with cross-origin POST as the CSRF vector (CWE-352)

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools build backend; pytest with pytest-asyncio (asyncio_mode=auto), pytest-cov, pytest-xdist; dev extras in pyproject.toml:184-194
O10_build.project_tests: tests/src/unit/test_settings_ui.py covers route registration (TestRouteRegistration, lines 380-416), save-body validation and policy endpoints; tests/addon/test_addon_structure.py:63-79 locks ingress/ingress_port/ingress_stream and the published 9583 port. At the pinned commit no test asserts any peer-address gate.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the peer check inside the shared handlers (or only to the write handlers named in the report, save_tools/policy_put_config/restart) and gate on X-Forwarded-For, leaving the bare-root "/" page and the read routes open while 403-ing the secret-path twins that direct and standalone clients depend on.
